Hořava–Lifshitz gravity | Hořava–Lifshitz gravity (or Hořava gravity) is a theory of quantum gravity proposed by Petr Hořava in 2009. The relativistic concept of time with its Lorentz invariance emerges at large distances.  The theory relies on the theory of foliations to produce its causal structure. The novelty of this approach, compared to previous approaches to quantum gravity such as Loop quantum gravity, is that it uses concepts from condensed matter physics such as quantum critical phenomena.
